tip.title: Pro-Tip
tip.text: "Hands-on experience" is highly valued by recruiters. Use it in your CV to describe internships, volunteer work, or practical projects.

tip.title: Pro-Tip: Precision Matters
tip.text: In a corporate environment, using "Remuneration" instead of "Salary" signals a higher level of professional literacy, especially during contract negotiations or formal interviews.

sections.title: 3. Auxiliary Adverbs
sections.description: Adverbs of degree or intensity function as auxiliary modifiers. In professional English, they elevate basic descriptions to precise, impactful statements.

points.title: Highly
examples: He is a highly effective leader.

points.title: Extremely
examples: Managing this project is extremely complex.

rows: He is a highly effective leader.
Managing this project is extremely complex.

tip.title: Pro-Tip: Precision
tip.text: Avoid overusing "very." Instead, use specific auxiliary adverbs like "consistently" to demonstrate reliability over time.

sections.title: Sentence Completion
sections.description: Choose the best word or phrase to complete each workplace sentence.

questions.prompt: "To succeed in marketing, you need to ________ a clear career path early on."
questions.explanation: Pursue a career path is the standard collocation for actively following a professional direction; trace does not express that goal.

questions.prompt: "Internships are the best way to gain ________ experience before graduating."
questions.explanation: Hands-on experience comes from doing practical work; theoretical and remote describe different ways of learning or working.

questions.prompt: "Our team is ________ motivated to achieve the annual targets."
questions.explanation: Highly motivated is the standard degree collocation; widely and absolutely do not normally modify motivated in this context.

questions.prompt: "Managing this project requires the ability to work well under ________."
questions.explanation: Work under pressure is the established expression for performing despite stress or deadlines; weight and control do not fit the collocation.

questions.prompt: "Many employees struggle to achieve a healthy work-life ________."
questions.explanation: Work-life balance is the established term for managing professional and personal demands; equality and status do not complete it.

questions.prompt: "You must ________ the deadline if you want to keep this client."
questions.explanation: Meet a deadline means complete work by the required time; catch and finish do not form the target collocation with deadline.

sections.title: Listening: A Competency-Based Interview
sections.description: Listen for the candidate's example, evidence and reflection.

audio.transcript: Could you tell us about a time when you had to manage conflicting priorities? Certainly. In my previous role, I was coordinating a product launch when a major client reported a technical problem. Both tasks were urgent, but I couldn't handle them effectively on my own. I first assessed the commercial impact and informed the launch team that our internal deadline might move by several hours. Then I brought together an engineer and an account manager to deal with the client issue while I continued preparing the launch materials. I scheduled brief updates every thirty minutes so that everyone had the same information. We resolved the fault before midday and launched the product that afternoon. The client later renewed its contract. Looking back, the key was not simply working faster; it was communicating the trade-offs clearly and giving each person a defined responsibility. If the same situation arose now, I would document the initial decision more carefully so that senior managers could review it afterwards.

gistQuestions.prompt: Which ability is the candidate mainly demonstrating?
gistQuestions.explanation: The example focuses on prioritisation, delegation and communication.

detailQuestions.explanation: The candidate scheduled updates every thirty minutes.

detailQuestions.prompt: What would the candidate improve next time?
options: Document the initial decision more carefully
detailQuestions.explanation: The reflection identifies documentation as the improvement.

tip.title: Listening Tip
tip.text: Interview answers often follow situation, action, result and reflection. Use that structure to organise your notes.

sections.title: Writing Part 4: Career Goals
sections.description: Write a short formal response using the vocabulary from this lesson.

prompt.situation: You are applying for an internship at an international company. Write a short message explaining why you want the position and what kind of experience you hope to gain.
prompt.referenceAnswer: I am applying for this internship because I want to gain hands-on experience in a professional environment. I am highly motivated, able to work under pressure, and eager to pursue a clear career path in international business.

tip.title: B2 Writing Tip
tip.text: Use precise collocations and one auxiliary adverb, such as highly motivated or consistently reliable, to raise the formality of your response.
